title: The Passive With Se: How Coffee Is Made

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive *se* from B1 Unit 6: *se* + a verb that agrees with the thing, when who does the action is unimportant or general (*se busca una persona*, *se buscan personas*). A process like coffee growing is told this way: the beans, the houses and the buses matter more than the people who handle them.

sections.title: Singular thing, singular verb; plural thing, plural verb
rows: El café se recoge a mano.
Los granos se despulpan, se lavan y se secan.
En los pueblos se conservan casas de bahareque.

items.spanish: El café se recoge a mano en laderas muy inclinadas.
items.english: The coffee is picked by hand on very steep slopes.

items.spanish: Después de la cosecha, los granos se secan al sol.
items.english: After the harvest, the beans are dried in the sun.

items.spanish: En el Eje Cafetero todavía se usan las chivas.
items.english: In the Eje Cafetero the chivas are still used.

items.spanish: En las fincas se explica cómo se produce el café.
items.english: On the farms they explain how coffee is produced.

sections.content: The verb agrees with the thing: *se recoge el café*, *se recogen los granos*. When you want to name who does the action, use the passive with *ser* instead (B1 Unit 18). Do not drop *se*: *los granos recogen a mano* would mean that the beans pick something.
